analysis.title: Market Internal Weekly: Special Q&A Edition; Amid News-Triggered Weakness, Real-Money Support Strengthened Further
key_insights: UBS US equity derivatives strategy keeps its bullish view. Near-term pressure may persist, but the setup turns increasingly bullish after mid-November, particularly after next week's anticipated IPO.

Real-money demand is strengthening: foreign-listed US ETF weekly inflows are +4.7x standard deviation, the strongest since Dec 2024. Foreigners bought almost 100% of days since October. UBS RMM clients bought the dip 75% of days and the rally 83% of days so far in Nov.
Target Date Fund inflows are +$38bn through Nov 12 (+$43bn as of Nov 10 in the model details), on track for one of the best inflow months of 2026.
Corporate buybacks return from blackout at $50-55bn per week for most weeks from next week to the first week of January. The model details list $35-55bn per week for this week and the next 7.
Three capitulation signals were seen on Nov 5: -$365bn excess sell flow, the largest retail selling since March 2020, and a VIX cross-asset rank above 95%.

HF and systematic positioning is washed out: Risk Control exposure is 57% (2%-tile vs 1Y, 24%-tile vs 5Y, lowest since Tariff). UBS PB L/S ratio is 7%-tile vs 1Y. CTA equity exposure is 9%-tile vs 1Y and turned negative this week, which has historically marked bottoms when real money is not selling.
Short interest is elevated: Russell 2000 at 10.1% (99%-tile vs 5Y), S&P 500 at 2.0% (94%-tile vs 5Y), Nasdaq 100 at 1.7% (89%-tile vs 5Y). UBS frames this as short-squeeze risk and a downside buffer.

On next week's anticipated IPO: pre-IPO liquidity selling should be largely behind the market. Across the four largest US IPOs relative to market cap since 2008 (Visa, GM, Facebook, SpaceX), SPX's average max drawdown in the three weeks before was -5.8%, against the recent -5.0%.
After the four prior IPOs, SPX rose in every case, averaging +9.5% in 3M. The IPO stocks were far more volatile, with average 3M low/high returns of -20.2%/+24.8%.

Retail tax-loss harvesting is likely underway, but UBS expects stock-specific selling rather than a broad-market headwind. Timing has spread through the year since 2019. December recorded net inflows in 4 of the last 6 years.

UBS does not expect a repeat of the 2018Q4 -20% SPX selloff, though it does not rule out more volatility. Market signals and systematic exposures resemble Nov 12, 2018, but real-money flow is much stronger across every measure.
UBS RMM clients have bought semiconductor stocks heavily over the last few days, including today, at a faster pace than ETFs.
Dealer gamma is short at -$0.37bn (11%-tile vs 5Y) as of Nov 11. SPX dealer gamma for options expiring from t+1 is bound between -$5bn and +$7bn (at 7750) across 7100-8100.
Risk Control scenario rebalancing: if SPX falls 3% in a day, expect to cut $50-55bn. A 2% fall implies a $20bn cut. A 1% fall implies a $5bn buy.

CTA triggers: ES1 has 3 close buy triggers (7688.5, 7708.3, 7709.8) and 1 sell trigger, an MT MA crossover expected by the end of this week. RTY1 has 5 close buy triggers from 2867.3 to 2923.9. NQ1 has no close triggers.
VIX fell to 17.5, leaving the VIX cross-asset rank at a moderate 48%, after it rose to 96% when VIX hit 28.2 last Thursday.

vol_and_positioning: VIX dropped to 17.5. VIX cross-asset rank is 48%, after reaching 96% when VIX was 28.2 last Thursday.
Dealer gamma is short at -$0.37bn (11%-tile vs 5Y) as of Nov 11. SPX dealer gamma from t+1 is between -$5bn and +$7bn (at 7750) across 7100-8100.
ETF option gamma risk proxies by open interest: SPY 32%-tile, QQQ 96%-tile, IWM 60%-tile vs 5Y. Top stock option OI is 27%-tile for S&P 500, 35%-tile for Nasdaq and 78%-tile for R2000.
Leveraged ETP AUM is $128bn (39%-tile vs 1Y). Rebalance sensitivity is about $6.4bn per 1% move, of which $4.7bn is Nasdaq/Tech.

VIX call/put ratio dropped to the 10%-tile vs 1Y. SPY, QQQ and IWM put/call ratios are at the 25%, 0% and 62%-tile vs 5Y. Top-50 S&P stock 110 call skew fell 3.4% on average (39%-tile vs 5Y), and only 22% of names have positive call skew.
UBS PB L/S gross leverage is at the 35%-tile vs 1Y and net at the 8%-tile. L/S ratio is 1.96x (7%-tile vs 1Y). Flow is still mostly selling at -0.6x standard deviation.
CFTC leveraged funds as of Nov 3 covered NQ shorts for the 6th straight week (97%-tile vs 5Y) and added to RTY shorts (42%-tile vs 5Y).
Risk Parity equity exposure is 29% (87%-tile vs 5Y) and bond exposure is 79% (48%-tile vs 5Y). Equity/bond correlations are -28% at 1M and -7% at 2M, against +25% at 6M and +27% at 1Y.

tension_points.bull_case: Real-money demand is strengthening, positioning is washed out, short interest is elevated and buybacks return. The four prior large IPOs were followed by SPX +9.5% on average in 3M.
tension_points.bear_case: Pre-IPO capital raising, tax-loss harvesting and news-triggered uncertainty may keep weighing on the market near term. A short-gamma dealer position and a CTA sell trigger add to the risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 3% one-day SPX drop would trigger a $50-55bn Risk Control cut. The CTA ES1 MT moving-average crossover sell trigger is expected by the end of this week.
